title: Ocean acidification
text: Roughly a quarter of the carbon dioxide released by human activity is absorbed by the oceans. Although this [[uptake|upt]] slows atmospheric warming, it comes [[at|a]] a cost. Dissolved carbon dioxide reacts [[with|wi]] seawater to form carbonic acid, [[thereby|the]] lowering the water's pH. The [[resulting|resu]] chemical shift reduces the availability [[of|o]] carbonate ions, [[which|wh]] corals, oysters, and many plankton [[require|req]] to build their shells and skeletons. [[Unless|Unl]] emissions decline, marine ecosystems [[dependent|depe]] on these organisms could be severely disrupted.
explanation: «this uptake» = esta absorción (sustantivo; resume la frase anterior). «comes at a cost» = tiene un precio (expresión fija). «reacts with» = reacciona con. «thereby lowering» = reduciendo así (thereby + -ing expresa consecuencia). «The resulting shift» = el cambio resultante (participio -ing como adjetivo). «the availability of». «ions, which corals … require»: relativo de objeto; «require» en plural porque el sujeto son corals, oysters y plankton. «Unless» = a menos que. «ecosystems dependent on» = dependientes de (adjetivo en -ent + on; no «dependence»). Truco: «Unless» ya es negativo; no lo confundas con «Until».

title: The mechanical clock
text: The mechanical clock, which appeared in European monasteries and town towers around 1300, transformed the way people understood time. Previously, the length [[of|o]] an hour had varied [[with|wi]] the seasons, [[since|si]] daylight was simply divided [[into|in]] twelve equal parts. Mechanical clocks, [[by|b]] contrast, struck hours of [[identical|iden]] length regardless of the [[season|sea]]. This [[innovation|innov]] gradually reshaped daily life: merchants [[began|be]] to schedule meetings precisely, and employers [[increasingly|increa]] measured work in hours rather than tasks.
explanation: «the length of an hour». «varied with the seasons» = variaba según las estaciones. «since» = porque (causa). «divided into» = dividido en. «by contrast» = en cambio. «identical length» = duración idéntica. «regardless of the season» = sin importar la estación. «This innovation» = este invento (sustantivo en -tion). «merchants began»: pasado, porque el resto del relato está en pasado (measured). «increasingly measured» = cada vez más medían (adverbio). Truco: en las colocaciones fijas (by contrast, regardless of, divided into) la preposición no se puede cambiar.

title: Fungal networks beneath forests
text: Beneath most forests lies an extensive web of fungal threads that connect the roots of neighboring trees. In this [[relationship|relati]], the fungi supply trees [[with|wi]] water and mineral nutrients, [[while|wh]] the trees provide sugars produced [[through|thr]] photosynthesis. Some researchers [[argue|ar]] that the network also allows [[established|estab]] trees to transfer carbon to [[younger|you]] seedlings, although this [[claim|cl]] remains [[controversial|contro]]. Critics point out that [[much|mu]] of the evidence comes from controlled experiments rather than mature forests.
explanation: «In this relationship» = en esta relación (sustantivo en -ship). «supply X with Y» = abastecer a X de Y. «while» = mientras que (contraste entre dos partes). «produced through photosynthesis» = mediante la fotosíntesis. «researchers argue that» = sostienen que. «established trees» = árboles ya asentados/adultos, frente a «younger seedlings» (comparativo). «this claim remains controversial» = esta afirmación sigue siendo polémica (adjetivo en -ial). «much of the evidence»: evidence es incontable, por eso «much» y no «many». Truco: incontable → much; contable → many.

title: Cognitive dissonance
text: When people hold two beliefs that contradict each other, they often experience an uncomfortable state that psychologists call cognitive dissonance. To reduce this [[tension|ten]], individuals may change one of their [[beliefs|bel]] or, more commonly, [[reinterpret|reint]] the evidence so that it [[appears|app]] consistent. In a classic [[experiment|exper]], participants who were paid very [[little|lit]] to describe a boring task as enjoyable later rated [[it|i]] more favorably than those paid generously. [[Apparently|Appar]], the poorly paid group, lacking an external [[justification|justif]] for their statement, [[adjusted|adju]] their attitudes instead.
explanation: «this tension» = esta tensión (sustantivo en -sion). «one of their beliefs»: one of + plural. «reinterpret» = reinterpretar (prefijo re-), en paralelo con «change» tras «may». «so that it appears consistent» = para que parezca coherente (3ª persona: -s). «a classic experiment». «paid very little» = muy poco (cantidad de dinero). «rated it» = la valoraron (it = la tarea). «Apparently» = al parecer. «an external justification» = justificación (sustantivo en -tion tras adjetivo). «adjusted» en pasado, como «rated». Truco: tras «an + adjetivo» va un sustantivo.

title: The Green Revolution
text: Between the 1940s and the 1970s, a series of agricultural innovations known as the Green Revolution dramatically increased grain production in many developing countries. High-yield [[varieties|vari]] of wheat and rice, combined [[with|wi]] chemical fertilizers and irrigation, enabled farmers to [[double|dou]] or even triple their harvests. [[Nevertheless|Nevert]], the gains were unevenly [[distributed|distr]]. Wealthier farmers, who [[could|co]] afford the necessary inputs, benefited the [[most|mo]], whereas smallholders often fell into debt. Moreover, intensive [[cultivation|culti]] depleted groundwater and degraded soils, [[raising|rai]] doubts about whether such [[productivity|produc]] could be sustained.
explanation: «High-yield varieties» = variedades de alto rendimiento (plural de variety: -ies). «combined with». «to double or even triple» = duplicar o incluso triplicar (verbos en paralelo). «Nevertheless» = sin embargo (concesión al inicio). «unevenly distributed» = repartidos de forma desigual (participio pasivo). «who could afford» = que podían permitirse. «benefited the most» = los que más se beneficiaron («the more» sería incorrecto). «intensive cultivation» = cultivo intensivo (sustantivo en -tion). «raising doubts» = planteando dudas (-ing de consecuencia). «such productivity» = tal productividad (sustantivo en -ity). Truco: «such» va con sustantivo; por eso «productivity» y no «productive».

title: Finding planets by their shadows
text: Most of the planets known to orbit other stars were not observed directly but inferred from subtle changes in starlight. When a planet passes in front of its star, it [[blocks|blo]] a tiny [[fraction|frac]] of the light, producing a [[periodic|peri]] dip in brightness. The [[depth|de]] of this dip reveals the planet's size, [[whereas|whe]] the interval between dips [[corresponds|corre]] to its orbital period. [[However|How]], the method works only [[if|i]] the orbit is aligned almost [[exactly|exa]] with our line of sight, [[which|wh]] means that most planetary systems remain invisible to it.
explanation: «it blocks» = bloquea (3ª persona -s). «a tiny fraction of» = una pequeñísima fracción de. «a periodic dip» = una caída periódica (adjetivo en -ic). «The depth of this dip» = la profundidad (sustantivo de deep). «whereas» = mientras que (contraste). «corresponds to» = corresponde a. «However» = sin embargo. «only if» = sólo si. «almost exactly» = casi exactamente (adverbio). «, which means that» = lo cual significa que (which se refiere a toda la frase). Truco: «which» tras coma puede resumir una oración completa.

title: The first writing
text: The earliest known writing system emerged in southern Mesopotamia more than five thousand years ago. Rather [[than|th]] recording speech or literature, the first [[inscriptions|inscri]] were administrative: they tracked quantities [[of|o]] grain, livestock, and labor owed to temple authorities. Scribes initially [[pressed|pre]] simple pictorial signs into wet clay, [[but|b]] over time these signs became [[progressively|progre]] abstract. [[Eventually|Event]], many symbols came to represent sounds [[instead|ins]] of objects, a [[development|devel]] that allowed writing to capture the [[structure|stru]] of spoken language.
explanation: «Rather than + -ing» = en lugar de. «the first inscriptions» = inscripciones (sustantivo en -tion, plural porque «were»). «quantities of grain». «pressed … into wet clay» = presionaban sobre arcilla húmeda (pasado). «, but over time» = pero con el tiempo. «progressively abstract» = cada vez más abstractos (adverbio ante adjetivo). «Eventually» = finalmente, con el tiempo (¡no «eventualmente»!). «instead of» = en lugar de. «a development that» = un avance (sustantivo en -ment). «the structure of spoken language». Truco: «eventually» es un falso amigo: significa «al final».

title: Invasive species on islands
text: Islands are especially vulnerable to invasive species, largely because their native animals evolved in isolation. Many island birds, [[for|f]] example, nest on the ground and show [[little|lit]] fear of predators, [[since|si]] none existed there for millions of years. When rats or cats [[arrive|arr]], often as stowaways on ships, [[such|su]] birds are easily captured. The [[consequences|conseq]] can be devastating: [[numerous|nume]] species have vanished [[within|wit]] decades of human contact. Eradication programs have [[succeeded|succ]] on some smaller islands, [[although|alth]] they are costly and require years of monitoring.
explanation: «for example» entre comas. «show little fear» = muestran poco miedo (fear es incontable → little). «since none existed» = ya que no existía ninguno (causa). «When rats or cats arrive»: presente en una verdad general. «such birds» = esas aves (such + plural). «The consequences» = consecuencias (sustantivo en -ence, plural por «can be»). «numerous species» = numerosas especies (adjetivo en -ous). «within decades of» = en pocas décadas tras. «have succeeded» = han tenido éxito (participio de succeed). «although» = aunque (concesión). Truco: los adjetivos en -ous (numerous, various, enormous) suelen ir delante de un sustantivo plural.

title: The Dust Bowl
text: During the 1930s, severe drought and destructive farming practices turned large areas of the American Great Plains into a region known as the Dust Bowl. In [[preceding|prec]] decades, settlers had plowed up the deep-rooted grasses [[that|th]] had held the soil in place. When rainfall [[declined|decl]], the exposed topsoil dried out [[and|a]] was carried away by powerful winds. Enormous dust storms [[darkened|dark]] the sky [[as|a]] far east as the Atlantic coast. Thousands [[of|o]] families abandoned their farms, [[migrating|migr]] westward in search of work. The disaster [[ultimately|ultim]] prompted the government to promote soil [[conservation|conser]] techniques.
explanation: «In preceding decades» = en las décadas anteriores (-ing como adjetivo). «the grasses that had held» = que habían sujetado (relativo de sujeto). «rainfall declined» = disminuyeron las lluvias (pasado). «dried out and was carried away»: dos verbos con el mismo sujeto. «darkened the sky» = oscurecieron (verbo en -en: dark → darken). «as far east as» = hasta tan al este como (estructura fija). «Thousands of families». «migrating westward» = emigrando hacia el oeste (-ing de acción simultánea). «ultimately» = en última instancia. «soil conservation» = conservación del suelo (sustantivo en -tion). Truco: el sufijo -en convierte adjetivos en verbos (dark → darken, wide → widen).

title: Comparative advantage
text: The theory of comparative advantage, first formulated by the economist David Ricardo, explains why countries benefit from trade even when one of them is more efficient at producing everything. [[Suppose|Sup]] that one nation can make both cloth and wine more [[cheaply|che]] [[than|th]] its neighbor. It may still gain by [[concentrating|concen]] on the good it produces most [[efficiently|effic]] [[relative|rela]] to the other, and importing the rest. What [[matters|mat]] is not absolute productivity [[but|b]] opportunity cost: the amount of one good that must be [[sacrificed|sacri]] in order to produce [[another|ano]].
explanation: «Suppose that» = supongamos que (imperativo para plantear un ejemplo). «more cheaply than» = más barato que (adverbio en -ly porque modifica a «make»). «by concentrating on» = concentrándose en (by + -ing = mediante). «most efficiently» = de la forma más eficiente (adverbio). «relative to» = en relación con. «What matters is» = lo que importa es (3ª persona -s). «not X but Y» = no X sino Y. «must be sacrificed» = debe sacrificarse (pasiva). «to produce another» = otro (un bien más). Truco: «not … but» se traduce por «no … sino».

title: Thawing permafrost
text: Permafrost, ground that remains frozen for at least two consecutive years, covers roughly a quarter of the land in the Northern Hemisphere. It [[retains|ret]] vast quantities of organic matter, [[accumulated|accum]] over thousands of years from plants [[and|a]] animals that never fully decomposed. As the Arctic [[warms|wa]], this material thaws and microbes begin [[to|t]] break it down, releasing carbon dioxide and methane. [[Because|Bec]] these gases trap heat, their release could [[further|fur]] accelerate warming, [[creating|crea]] what scientists call a feedback loop. Thawing ground also destabilizes roads and buildings, [[posing|pos]] serious challenges [[for|f]] northern communities.
explanation: «It retains» = retiene/conserva (3ª persona -s). «organic matter, accumulated over» = acumulada (participio pasivo). «plants and animals». «As the Arctic warms» = a medida que el Ártico se calienta (verbo, no «warmth»). «begin to break it down» = empiezan a descomponerla. «Because these gases trap heat» = como estos gases retienen calor. «could further accelerate» = podría acelerar aún más (further = más, adicionalmente). «creating» y «posing»: -ing de consecuencia («posing challenges» = planteando retos). «challenges for» = retos para. Truco: «pose a challenge/problem/risk» es una colocación muy académica.

title: Toolmaking crows
text: New Caledonian crows are among the few animals known to manufacture tools rather than simply use objects they find. In the wild, they [[fashion|fas]] twigs and leaves [[into|in]] hooks that [[enable|ena]] them to extract insects from crevices. [[Remarkably|Remar]], laboratory studies have shown that some individuals [[can|c]] bend a straight piece of wire to [[retrieve|retr]] food they could [[not|n]] otherwise reach. Such [[behavior|beha]] was once considered [[uniquely|uniq]] human, [[and|a]] its discovery in birds has prompted researchers to reconsider which cognitive abilities depend on a large, primate-like brain.
explanation: «fashion X into Y» = dar forma de Y a X (fashion como verbo). «into hooks»: into indica transformación. «enable them to extract» = les permiten extraer (enable + objeto + to). «Remarkably» = sorprendentemente (adverbio de comentario). «can bend» = pueden doblar. «to retrieve food» = para recuperar/alcanzar comida. «could not otherwise reach» = no podrían alcanzar de otro modo. «Such behavior» = tal comportamiento (ortografía de EE. UU.; «behaviour» tendría 9 letras). «uniquely human» = exclusivamente humano. «, and its discovery». Truco: «otherwise» = de otro modo; suele ir con un modal (could, would).
